a hybrid nanostructure consisting of a silver island associated with a silver nanoparticle is an excellent plasmonic platform for the enhancement of fluorescence, and the coupling plasmon between these two nanostructures can be tuned by adjusting the size and shape of the island.
the coupling plasmon can enhance the fluorescence of a hybrid nanostructured composed of a silver island (SI), which is modeled as an oblateness spheroid, and a silver nanoparticle (NP).
the coupling plasmon between SI and SNP is responsible for MEF effect and the induced optical force allows the SNP to be attracted by SI to form a smaller gap.

the MEF effect on the hybrid nanostructure, which can be used as a potential tool for biosensing.
the plasmon coupling effect of the hybrid structure on MEF and the induced optical force between the components.
the coupling plasmon effect of a hybrid nanostructured and its application in MEF, which is of great significance for the design of a MEF device.

the hybrid nanostructure has the potential to be applied as a novel MEF platform.

the coupling plasmon between the two nanostructures can be utilized to achieve a broadband and tunable MEF effect.
the hybrid nanostructure has the potential to achieve a high fluorescence enhancement on various molecules with different excitation spectra.
